hate_speech_law: Hateful public speech about a group shouldn't be a crime unless it threatens or incites violence, as now.
Only the most extreme hateful public speech, like calling a group subhuman, should be a crime.
Hateful public speech about people's race, religion, sexual orientation or gender identity should be punishable with fines or jail.
hateful_speaker_response: The right response to legal but hateful speech is more speech, not trying to silence the speaker.
Criticism and boycotts are fair responses, but the speaker shouldn't lose their job or platform.
Platforms, venues and employers should drop people who say hateful things, even when it's legal.
The law should punish hateful speech toward a racial or religious group.

A public university shouldn't allow this talk: {case}.
flag_burning: Burning the American flag in protest should be legal, as protected speech.
Flag burning should be legal, but cities can ban open fires in certain places for safety.
The Constitution should be amended so flag burning can be banned.
protest_masks: Wearing a mask to hide your identity at a protest should be legal.
Wearing a mask at a protest should be illegal only while committing a crime.
Wearing a mask to hide your identity at any protest should be illegal.
campus_encampments: Public universities should allow peaceful protest camps on campus.
Public universities should allow protest camps only for a limited time, in designated areas.
Public universities should remove protest camps right away, even peaceful ones.
gov_misinformation: Government shouldn't judge what's true online at all.
Government can publish its own corrections to false claims, but nothing more.
Government can flag posts it considers false, but can't require platforms to remove them.
Government agencies should decide what's false on topics like health and elections, and platforms should have to remove it.
misinfo_penalty: There shouldn't be new penalties for spreading false information beyond existing fraud and defamation laws.
Knowingly spreading false claims about when, where or how to vote should be punishable, but nothing else new.
Knowingly spreading harmful false claims should be punishable with fines or jail.
jawboning: Government officials should never pressure social media companies over legal speech.
Officials can ask platforms to remove posts only for clear legal violations, like threats.
Officials can ask platforms to remove legal posts, but every request must be made public.
Officials can ask platforms to remove legal posts they consider harmful, and the companies decide.
library_book_decisions: School librarians, using professional standards, should decide whether a challenged book stays.
A committee of librarians, teachers and parents should decide whether a challenged book stays.
The elected school board should decide whether a challenged book stays.
One parent's objection should be enough to pull a book from the shelves while it's reviewed.
library_explicit: High school libraries should freely carry literary novels with explicit sex scenes.
High school libraries can carry those novels, but students need a parent's permission to check them out.
High school libraries shouldn't carry novels with explicit descriptions of sex.
employer_speech: The law should stop private employers from firing workers for legal political speech outside work.
Employers can fire workers for political speech outside work only if it directly harms the business.
Private employers should be free to fire workers for political views they express outside work.
employer_speech_cases: An employer shouldn't be able to fire someone for this: {case}.
An employer should be able to fire someone for this: {case}.
defamation_public_figures: Public figures should keep needing to prove an outlet knew a story was false or recklessly ignored the truth.
It should be somewhat easier for public figures to sue news outlets over false stories.
Public figures should only have to prove a story was false and harmful to win a lawsuit.
public_broadcasting: The federal government should fund public radio and TV more than it has in the past.
The federal government should fund public radio and TV about as it has in the past.
The federal government shouldn't fund public broadcasting.
campus_speech_codes: Public universities should be able to discipline students for offensive speech, even when it isn't a threat or harassment.
Public universities can discipline offensive speech only when it's repeated and aimed at a specific person.
Public universities shouldn't discipline students for offensive speech that isn't a threat or harassment.
